Subject: BridgeBroker encrypted relay — initial integration packet

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking the time in the partnership intake last week. Per our call, attached is a compact integration packet for BridgeBroker — our encrypted evidence-relay layer that partners use to push SOC2/pentest artifacts into customer GRC buckets while maintaining end-to-end encryption and HSM-backed keying.

What’s included in this email:
- BridgeBroker-integration-spec.pdf (overview + API surfaces)
- runtime-capabilities.csv (typical throughput/batching numbers for 1–8 GPUs)

High level asks from our side:
1) Confirm whether Redwood can support an HSM-backed wrap/unwrap flow (KMIP or AWS KMS + external key wrap) for transferred artifacts.
2) Confirm required audit/logging fields so we can emit a compatible event stream.
3) Share any minimum SLA/pen-test acceptance criteria you require for partner connectors.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30 min tech sync with your security/assurance leads this week.

Best,
Michael Torres
Partnerships, SecuBridge
Attachments: BridgeBroker-integration-spec.pdf (PDF), runtime-capabilities.csv (CSV)

Looping in Laura (partner ops) for procurement and connector packaging, Marcus (security) for KMS/audit needs, and Soojin (assurance) for pen-test/acceptance gating. Suggested next steps:

- Partner SOW template + doc to align on who hosts keys and retention
- Mapping of your event fields to Redwood’s audit schema (we’ll share a mapping doc)

Propose Wed 3/17 11:00am PT for a short call — does that work? I’ll prep a short agenda: 1) key management model, 2) audit schema, 3) acceptance criteria + timeline.

Also please share any sample connector packaging (tar/zip) and a contact at PenSafe Labs if you’ll need a pen-test handoff.

— Hannah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, soojin.lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <partner@secubridge.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 13:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeBroker encrypted relay — initial integration packet

Thanks Hannah — quick technical note from security:

1) KMS/HSM model
- For Hosted: we can accept artifacts encrypted with a partner-wrapped key if partner provides key-wrap metadata (alg, key-id). For Dedicated/Private: customer-managed KMS is required; we need key material never exported.
- Preferred: KMIP or AWS KMS with external key wrap (RSA-OAEP or AES-KWP).

2) Audit/event schema
- Required fields: event_id, timestamp (RFC3339), artifact_id, source_partner, customer_id, transfer_status, hash_sha256, key_wrap_method, envelope_version
- Optional: origin_ip, agent_version

3) Pen-test/acceptance gating
- Connector must pass: static code scan, SCA, and a blackbox transfer test (artifact replay + integrity verification).
- Provide a test bundle and a short threat-model doc. If partner uses PenSafe Labs, we’ll accept their report + remediation plan.

I attached a short checklist with KMS requirements — kms-reqs.md.

Marcus Lin
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: kms-reqs.md (MD)
